<!-- /sc:issue feature template (simple). Copy to <D>/issue-body.md and fill every placeholder in place. Keep every heading. Write "Not known yet" under a heading when the description and the codebase pass give nothing; never invent a fact. The exception is ## Priority, ## Fix approach and ## Test plan: fill them at every depth from the codebase pass, never write "Not known yet" there, and state any assumption in the section (rules in refs/create.md). -->

## Feature Summary
Protect the coordinator's Orca message watch from Claude Code's low-memory background-command cleanup. Separately, measure what should be stopped or limited instead, recommend a policy, and raise follow-up issues for anything to build.

## Problem Statement
A developer's coordinator lost its background message watch under critical memory pressure. Claude told the model not to restart it automatically, so the coordinator stopped receiving messages. This stops a background command, not a Claude session.
Claude Code 2.1.331 applies this rule only when all conditions hold: runtime pressure is `critical`; no session input for 30 minutes; no turn or helper agents running; `/proc/meminfo` has `MemAvailable` below both 10% of `MemTotal` and 4 GiB; and no earlier pressure stop in 30 minutes unless terminal input occurred since. The log is `LocalShellTask <id>: reaped under critical memory pressure after <n>m idle`. Its notice says to start Claude with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=1`; setting it inside an already running Claude does not work. The switch protects every background command in that session, not just the watch.
The watch is `orca orchestration check --wait --types status,dispatch,worker_done,merge_ready,escalation,handoff,decision_gate,question,heartbeat --timeout-ms 300000 --json`. It ends and is started again every five minutes. Measured real memory (PSS, which apportions shared memory) was about 33 MB per watch versus 110 MB in RSS; it stayed flat over 90 seconds. Four plain Orca calls each peaked at 109 MB for 0.2 seconds because each loads the Orca runtime. Stopping the watch recovers little memory but breaks coordination.
The same workspace's 12 Claude sessions, including helper processes, held 0.44-0.62 GB each (about 0.53 GB average), whether Orca marked them working or done. Claude itself held 250-400 MB, the Playwright plugin server about 107 MB per session, and codegraph servers 50-190 MB; idle CPU was 0.2-0.8% of a core each. Issue #648 measured codegraph first-index peaks of 3.6-4.0 GiB per new checkout: ten concurrent builds reduced available memory by about 34 GiB and doubled build time. The workspace had no memory cap (`memory.max=max`, no limit in the Coder template); its roughly 9 GB was part of roughly 49 GB host use, with 77-80 GB host memory shared across workspaces and 4.5 of 5.3 GB swap used. These are starting measurements, not a universal stopping policy. Source for runtime behavior and measurements: orchestrator's verified investigation, 2026-11-24, including the installed Claude program at `/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.22.2/lib/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe`.

## User Story
As a coordinator operator, I want its message watch to survive Claude's low-memory cleanup so that messages keep reaching the coordinator, and I want measured evidence before deciding which other processes to stop.

## Proposed Solution
**Part 1, change:** pass `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=1` in the environment before starting the coordinator's Claude process. Decide and document whether this applies only to coordinator launches or all ccsession launches. Prefer a launch-time environment assignment over relying on settings whose timing is unverified. Do not solve this by telling the model to restart a command against Claude's notice.
**Part 2, research:** compare idle or finished sessions, open Playwright browsers, concurrent codegraph first-index builds, and a per-workspace memory cap under representative load. Measure memory actually recovered or peak memory avoided against work interrupted, recovery cost, and host impact. Recommend what to stop, limit or leave alone, with thresholds and follow-up issues; do not implement that broader policy in this issue.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A newly launched coordinator Claude has `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=1` in its initial process environment. The launch path and scope decision are recorded, including the session-wide effect and treatment of existing sessions.
- [ ] Automated launch tests cover the chosen scope and new/resumed sessions; a live coordinator proof checks only this variable in `/proc/<pid>/environ`, without exposing other environment values, and verifies message delivery over at least two five-minute watch cycles.
- [ ] A research report contains reproducible under-load comparisons for all four candidates, before/after memory and work impact, a ranked recommendation and its limitations, and links to follow-up issues for proposed implementation. It distinguishes host memory pressure from workspace use and PSS from RSS.
- [ ] Tests for the touched area, lint, formatting and synchronization checks pass; evidence and remaining uncertainties are linked.

## Out of Scope
Changing Claude Code itself; automatic watch restarts that disregard its notice; implementing a session reaper, browser cleanup, index scheduler or workspace memory cap before the research and follow-up decisions. Existing sessions are not retroactively changed by a launch fix.

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)
- `src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/ccsession`: sources the user environment before launch (`origin/master`, lines 1080-1086); exports launch identity at 2412-2438; executes Claude through untagged, resumed and new-session branches at 2440-2451 and 2498-2519. Put shared launch protection before these branches, after environment/profile setup. `src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/README.md` documents the chosen behavior.
- `src/superclaude/cli/user_settings_defaults.json:10-14` on `origin/master`: the defaults `env` block does not contain the switch. Whether Claude applies settings `env` before this rule is **unverified**, so it is an alternative requiring proof, not an established fix.
- `src/superclaude/hooks/scripts/codegraph-session-start.sh:21-31` on `origin/master`: checks this checkout's database then starts a detached first index; it has no cross-checkout concurrency limit. Research target only in this issue. Existing test surfaces include `tests/unit/test_ccsession_tag.py`, `tests/unit/test_ccsession_tiers.py` and `tests/unit/test_install_ccsession.py`.
Codegraph: index_state=fresh, checked_at=2026-11-24T17:06:48Z; degraded: graph:unlisted. Access was CLI only; codegraph/auggie MCP tools were unavailable. The no-depth `/sc:analyze` pass used Glob, Grep, Read and line-numbered `git show origin/master:<path>` for source evidence rather than graph lookups.

## Related Issues/PRs
[#648](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/648) (closed first-index memory measurements), [#716](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/716) and [#717](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/717) (coordinator features), and [#354](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/354) (v5.0.0 impact runbook). Related, not duplicates. Related pull requests: Not known yet.

## Priority
High: the rule's **other work is blocked** trigger applies because the coordinator stops receiving messages after its watch is stopped.

## Fix approach
Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: master.
Commands, in order: `/sc:analyze src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/` (also inspect the settings defaults and codegraph hook above), then `/sc:workflow "Protect the coordinator message watch and measure memory-pressure alternatives"`, then `/sc:implement <generated-plan-path>` for the launch change, controlled measurements and recommendation, then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`. Use `/sc:issue --create "<measured follow-up proposal>"` for each implementation recommendation. Paths in angle brackets are replaced with the actual generated artifacts; no broad cleanup is authorized by this sequence.
Steps, in order:
- Step 1: Trace the real coordinator launch through ccsession and record the scope choice in the generated plan. **Assumption to validate:** ccsession is the coordinator's launch entry point. Prefer its pre-exec environment; use coordinator-only protection if a reliable role signal is verified, otherwise explicitly document a decision to protect all ccsession launches. Do not infer roles from session labels. If choosing the installer settings instead, prove its timing first; inspect `src/superclaude/cli/user_settings_defaults.json` and its installer before changing them.
- Step 2: Change `src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/ccsession` and its README; export the switch after configuration and before every applicable Claude exec branch. Document the session-wide effect, explicit override behavior and need to launch a new Claude process. Add launch tests in `tests/unit/test_ccsession_tag.py` and `tests/unit/test_ccsession_tiers.py`; include installer tests only if that route changes. Run `make sync-dev`; do not edit generated `.claude/` mirrors as source.
- Step 3: Launch a fresh coordinator and inspect only the named switch in `/proc/<pid>/environ` for its actual Claude PID. Check the watch completes and is renewed across two cycles and receives a test message. Do not force critical pressure on a shared host. In an isolated test environment, exercise the verified cleanup prerequisites with and without protection, or explicitly record why this pressure-path check could not be run.
- Step 4: Measure each candidate under comparable load in a safe test workspace: idle/finished session process trees, open browsers separately from their Playwright server, serial versus concurrent first-index builds, and capped versus uncapped workspace memory. Record baseline/peak/after PSS, RSS, available host memory, cgroup use, swap, CPU, elapsed time and recovery/work loss; repeat and identify sample counts. A cap is containment, not itself a process to kill: evaluate its out-of-memory failures and effect on neighboring workspaces. Use #648 as a baseline, not proof of today's result. Write the recommendation in the generated task package and file implementation follow-ups.

## Test plan
- Tests to add or change: extend the fake-Claude launch harness in `tests/unit/test_ccsession_tag.py` and `tests/unit/test_ccsession_tiers.py` to capture only the new non-secret switch. Cover fresh/resumed and tagged/untagged launches, model/profile/tier variants, configuration loading, override policy and unaffected utility commands. If scope is coordinator-only, verify ordinary launches remain unchanged. If settings are changed, add merge/idempotence coverage for existing user settings as well.
- Regression gate: from the IronClaude checkout run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ccsession_tag.py tests/unit/test_ccsession_tiers.py tests/unit/test_install_ccsession.py`, plus any newly affected tests; `uv run pytest`; `uv run ruff check .`; `uv run ruff format --check .`; and `make verify-sync` after `make sync-dev`. Record results rather than assuming they pass.
- How a reviewer verifies: inspect only `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP` in the newly launched Claude's `/proc/<pid>/environ` using an exact-name filter and expect `=1`; never print the full environment. Match the PID to the coordinator, verify watch renewal and message delivery, and review any isolated pressure-path evidence or stated gap. The research report must provide commands, versions, workload, sample counts, process attribution, units, before/peak/after measurements, shared-host limitations, disruption/recovery costs, thresholds, alternatives rejected with reasons, and linked follow-up issues. **Assumption:** controlled load/pressure testing is available in an isolated workspace; otherwise report the missing experiment and do not claim pressure survival was demonstrated.

| 21 | "Issue #648 measured codegraph first-index peaks of 3.6-4.0 GiB per new checkout: ten concurrent builds reduced available memory by about 34 GiB and doubled build time" | UNVERIFIED here | The numbers live in closed issue #648, which this check did not re-read; the repo hook (row 7) shows the mechanism (one detached `codegraph init` per checkout, no limit). ## Claimed by @clayphi

- **ClickUp:** skipped (no_workspace)
- **Accuracy check:** current (see the accuracy-check comment on this issue)

### Summary

Part 1 puts `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=1` into the environment of the coordinator's Claude process at launch, so Claude Code's low-memory cleanup no longer stops the coordinator's Orca message watch, and records whether that covers only coordinator launches or every ccsession launch. Part 2 measures what should be stopped or limited instead when a workspace runs low on memory (idle or finished sessions, open Playwright browsers, concurrent codegraph first-index builds, a per-workspace memory cap) and ends with a ranked recommendation and follow-up issues, without building that policy.

#### Concrete next steps

In `src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/ccsession`, add one `export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=...` after the identity block (`:2438`) and before `:2440`; document it in `src/superclaude/skills/ccsession-tag/README.md` (session-wide effect, new Claude process needed, `ic` and hand-started Claude not covered).

title: [FEATURE] Stop Claude Code from killing the coordinator's message watch under low memory, and research what to stop instead
